statement: A read that failed and a canvas that is genuinely empty must never be represented by the same value.

body.problem: The shipped canvas returned [] when a read failed, so one 503 on open followed by one save overwrote a term of a student's work with a single entry.
body.mechanism: readCanvas returns {ok:true,artifacts} or {ok:false,reason}. There is no catch that turns an outage into a value.
body.whenNotToUse: Nowhere. This is an invariant of the product, not a technique to be weighed.
failureModes: any code path that treats an error as an absence
a caller that checks .length before it checks .ok

evidence.symbol: LAW D — "I could not read it" and "there is nothing here" are different answers

evidence.measurement: 12 real lessons on a canvas; API stopped; the page said "the canvas could not be read (500). Nothing is lost." and wrote nothing; server restarted; one save produced 13 rows with question 1 still at seq 1. The shipped code would have left exactly 1.

falsifiedBy: A canvas where a failed read and an empty canvas produce the same observable state on screen.
